Yes, I finished important work.
Fine, go work on your project further.
Our salaries were cut because of you!
They cut it exactly in half.
What? Why because of me?
All the money went to your project.
Lena's husband is actually disabled.
They pay him very tiny pennies.
I knew absolutely nothing!
Now all employees will suffer.
I will go to the dean right now.
I will sort out this situation.
Try, if they believe you.

Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще').

examples.trans: I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Disbelief. Core Russian part meaning 'yes' in everyday speech.

In a list or a story. Core Russian adv meaning 'next; further' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А дальше? Я очень волнуюсь, я к этому не приспособлена.
examples.trans: And then what? I'm very nervous, I'm not cut out for this.

meanings.note: 'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: The money is on the table.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: short form: ты довольна? = are you happy?

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?

meanings.en: to finish, to end, to complete
meanings.note: + acc. or infinitive. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'кончить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to finish, to complete', paired with 'заканчивать'.

examples.trans: I want to finish what I started.

examples.text: Был неправ. Простите. Я хочу закончить начатое.
examples.trans: I was wrong. Forgive me. I want to finish what I started.

meanings.note: жить на зарплату = to live on one's salary

examples.text: Эдуард Владимирович учёный, и он живёт на зарплату.
examples.trans: Eduard Vladimirovich is a scholar, and he lives on a salary.

meanings.note: A fact or a person. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'because of; from behind' in everyday speech.
+ genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'because of; from behind' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Из-за вашей Лёли весь класс зовёт меня врунишкой!
examples.trans: Because of your Lyolya the whole class calls me a little liar!
We were late because of the rain.

examples.text: А трава в мешках сгорела. Из-за вас!
examples.trans: And the herbs in the sacks burned. Because of you!

meanings.note: Animate masculine noun. Common masculine noun meaning 'disabled person' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Пьяный за рулём врезался в общество слепых! В инвалидов!
examples.trans: Drunk at the wheel, he crashed into the Society for the Blind! Into disabled people!

examples.text: В доме есть пандус для инвалидов.
examples.trans: The building has a ramp for disabled people.

meanings.note: + dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'to, towards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.en: kopeck, one hundredth of a rouble
meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'kopeck' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'kopeck' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Пятьсот. А у меня ни копейки.
examples.trans: Five hundred. And I haven't got a penny.

Мой муж = my husband. Common masculine noun meaning 'husband' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Nina, pour your husband a drink. We've got something to celebrate!

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Ну, папа!. Core Russian part meaning 'well; come on' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
For masculine and neuter things. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.
платить за + accusative = to pay for

examples.text: А вашу работу вернуть можно. И мы хорошо платим.
examples.trans: But we can get your job back for you. And we pay well.

meanings.note: + dative of the person: поверить ему

examples.text: Со своего телефона? И все поверили?
examples.trans: From your own phone? And everyone believed it?

meanings.note: On foot. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go (set off)', paired with 'идти'.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.en: to try, to taste (food or drink)
meanings.note: + accusative. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пробовать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to try, to taste', paired with 'пробовать'.

+ infinitive. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пробовать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to try, to taste', paired with 'пробовать'.

examples.trans: Try the tea with bread rings.

meanings.note: Asks about the reason. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чему').

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: A plan or piece of work. Common masculine noun meaning 'project' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The project is at a standstill.

examples.text: Давайте так: два дня. Или мы переводим проект в Калугу.
examples.trans: Here's what we'll do: two days. Or we move the project to Kaluga.

meanings.note: 'на работе' = at work. Common feminine noun meaning 'work, job' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'work, job' in everyday Russian.
'один раз' = once, 'два раза' = twice

разобраться.gloss: to sort out, to figure out

meanings.en: to sort out, to settle, to deal with
meanings.note: мы сами разберёмся = we'll sort it out ourselves

В + prepositional. Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'обраться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to sort out, to figure out', paired with 'разбираться'.

examples.text: Аникеев, иди к себе, а мы разберёмся.
examples.trans: Anikeev, go to your room, and we'll sort this out.

examples.text: Ну да, это понятно. Потом разберёмся.
examples.trans: Well yes, that's understandable. We'll sort it out later.

meanings.note: Borrowed from Latin agent/instrument noun in '-tor' ('ректор'). Common masculine noun meaning 'rector, university president' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: But you're the rector of the university!

examples.text: Но ты же ректор! У тебя есть какие-то возможности.
examples.trans: But you're the rector! You have some possibilities.

meanings.note: ровно десять секунд = exactly ten seconds
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Like a real man, exactly ten seconds.
They cut it exactly in half.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Borrowed via French/German from Medieval Latin 'situatio' (position, state of affairs, from 'situs').

examples.trans: This is a very complicated situation.

examples.text: Да никуда я не пряталась! Я контролировала ситуацию.
examples.trans: I wasn't hiding anywhere! I was controlling the situation.

meanings.note: Совершенно верно = quite right. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овершенно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town.
This is a completely new car.

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города. И предложение у меня к вам такое.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town. And my offer to you is this.

meanings.note: Совсем не. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овсем').
Совсем не. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овсем').

examples.text: Я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: That's not what I mean at all.

examples.text: Нет, Вика, я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: No, Vika, that's not what I mean at all.

meanings.note: Person working in an organization. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'отрудник'). Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'employee, staff member' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Why are you mistreating our staff?
All staff members gathered in the conference hall.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'традать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to suffer', paired with 'пострадать'.

examples.trans: People are suffering because of him.

examples.text: Ну и что? Он должен страдать, а нам нужна информация.
examples.trans: So what? He is supposed to suffer, and we need the information.

meanings.note: To someone you call ты. Core Russian det meaning 'your (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: As opposed to before. Core Russian adv meaning 'now (from now on)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

Просить у кого. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

уйти.gloss: to leave, to go away (on foot)

Budgets or salaries. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'резать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to cut, slash, reduce', paired with 'урезать'.

They cut it exactly in half.

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.
